chunks: Among them is Zu al-Isba' al-Adwani.
Abu Hatim said: He lived for three hundred years, and he was one of the kings of the Arabs in the period of Jahiliyyah (Pre-Islamic ignorance), and his reports, poems, and judgments are well known.

key_terms.أَبُو حَاتِمٍ: Abu Hatim (the source cited for the lifespan)

ai.seo_question: Who was Zu al-Isba' al-Adwani and how long did he live?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this passage highlights Zu al-Isba' al-Adwani as a prominent Pre-Islamic Arab ruler whose three-century lifespan exemplifies the phenomenon of *ghayba* (occultation or long life) among the Arabs. His enduring legacy, preserved through his poetry and judicial rulings, underscores the continuity of wisdom and governance in the Jahiliyyah period, serving as a historical precursor to the era of the Imams.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: According to Abul Hatim, he attained an age of 300 years. He was an Arab king during the period of Jahiliyya. His reports, poems and judgments are well known.
